QCNPTEXI: Achtemeier argues that the church neglects the Old Testament in the pulpit and shows preachers how to recover it. 3TQAVK7E: A companion to her earlier book, this volume takes on Old Testament passages that preachers usually avoid because they are violent, puzzling or morally troubling. 3KT7WZEP: Adamo studies how African Indigenous (Independent) Churches read the Bible: as a source of power for healing, protection and success, often in ways that echo traditional African practices. DT9N2EZK: Adamo surveys the Old Testament's references to Cush, Egypt and other African peoples and places. He argues that Africa and Africans played a larger and more positive role in ancient Israel's history than Western scholarship has usually recognised.
BMG3R2UG: A collection of essays setting out the aims and methods of African biblical hermeneutics. Adamo argues for reading Scripture from the African context and for the African context, drawing on African culture, experience and needs, including the use of the Psalms for healing and protection.
BNM4FIGC: An introductory social research methods textbook built around published studies. Each chapter explains a method (sampling, measurement, surveys, experiments, interviews, observation and analysis) by walking through how real researchers designed and carried out a particular study.
HFDSWNCZ: Agar's classic introduction to doing ethnography, written from his own fieldwork experience. He describes the ethnographer as a "professional stranger" who learns a community's way of life, and covers getting access, building relationships, fieldwork methods and writing up. The second edition adds reflection on how the field has changed since the book first appeared.
BEF6CEIF: A philosophical study of the foundations of African theology. Aja examines how African traditional thought, worldview and concepts of God and personhood can shape a theology that is both Christian and authentically African.
3TFTB2Z4: Åkerlund develops a phenomenology of leadership in Pentecostal churches, drawing on interviews with Pentecostal leaders and on Pentecostal theology. He shows how Pentecostals understand leadership as charismatic and Spirit-led, yet shaped by community, calling and practical wisdom, and proposes a model of leadership for the movement.
RB8J3QDX: An evangelical reference dictionary on Genesis to Deuteronomy. Its articles cover the books themselves, their major themes, people and places, their ancient Near Eastern background and the history of their interpretation, with bibliographies for further study.
U6MDJ4CX: A one-volume reference work on biblical theology. It has three parts: essays on the nature and method of biblical theology, articles on the theology of each section and book of the Bible, and articles tracing major themes (such as covenant, kingdom and temple) across the whole canon.
VN5N3FGM: Anderson's standard introduction to the history and theology of global Pentecostal and Charismatic Christianity. He traces its many origins, including in Africa, Asia and Latin America and not only Azusa Street, and discusses its theology, its approach to mission and the Spirit, and its social impact. The second edition updates both the data and the discussion.
4FT2MJX5: A textbook for Christian education. Contributors set out its biblical, theological, historical, philosophical and psychological foundations, and then apply them to teaching in the church across age groups and settings.
NHK2B3DD: An anthology of ancient Near Eastern texts in translation for students of the Old Testament, covering myths, epics, laws, letters, royal inscriptions, prayers and wisdom. Each text is introduced and linked to the biblical passages it helps illuminate.
QNU4RUM7: Specialists introduce the peoples and cultures surrounding ancient Israel, including Egyptians, Hittites, Canaanites, Phoenicians, Arameans, Assyrians, Babylonians and Persians. Each chapter covers history, religion and culture and then shows the relevance for reading the Old Testament.
5IADPXFP: An evangelical reference dictionary on the Old Testament historical books, Joshua to Esther. Its articles cover the books, their history and archaeology, people, places, themes and interpretive approaches, with bibliographies.
4XQXE8EA: A comprehensive handbook on ethnography across the social sciences. Specialist chapters cover its intellectual roots, its use in different fields, fieldwork methods, analysis and writing, and the ethical and political debates surrounding it.
NWVTANAP: A textbook introducing interdisciplinary studies. Augsburg explains what disciplines are, why some problems need more than one, and how to integrate insights from several fields. It encourages students to see themselves as interdisciplinary thinkers and learners.
EPGN99FV: Autry, a former corporate chief executive, presents servant leadership as practical and effective in business. He argues that leaders succeed by serving their people: being authentic, vulnerable, accepting, present and useful, and creating conditions in which others can do their best work.
UA9HQMTK: An extensive bibliography of the literature on open access to scholarly publishing. Bailey organises sources on its history, journals, repositories, mandates, economics and legal issues for researchers and librarians.
FJ7H8TM9: Baker surveys the main ways scholars have understood the relationship between the Old and New Testaments, including approaches built on Christology, typology, promise and fulfilment, salvation history and continuity and discontinuity. He then offers his own synthesis of how the two Testaments form one Bible.
79XHCGRU: A survey of the state of Old Testament scholarship at the end of the twentieth century. Leading evangelical scholars review recent work on each major area, including archaeology, history, the Pentateuch, the prophets, wisdom literature and Old Testament theology.
G35ZH8PQ: Bantu challenges the idea that Christianity is a Western religion. He traces how the early church spread across Africa, Asia and the Middle East and argues that its global, multi-ethnic identity is original to the faith, and that this matters for the church's witness today.
6HGXFP2A: A practical guide for students starting research in theology. It explains how to choose and narrow a topic, use libraries and databases, find and assess theological sources, take notes and organise and write a research paper.
BCFGPHSH: Barrett's classic study of the Holy Spirit in the Synoptic Gospels. He examines the passages that refer to the Spirit, such as Jesus' conception, baptism, temptation and exorcisms, and asks why the Gospels say comparatively little about the Spirit. He explains this mainly through the early church's eschatological expectations.
JEAWHU2B: Barton writes for leaders who are tired or spiritually depleted. She uses Moses' life to show how practices like solitude, silence, discernment, community and rhythms of rest can keep a leader's soul alive under the pressures of ministry.
SGEPDR98: Beale's handbook teaches the method of studying the New Testament's quotations of and allusions to the Old Testament. He explains how to identify a use, analyse its original and new contexts and understand the hermeneutical assumptions behind it, illustrating each step with examples.
5D2F9ZJI: A large one-volume commentary that goes through the New Testament book by book and discusses each quotation of, and major allusion to, the Old Testament. For each passage it treats the original context, its use in Jewish tradition, and how and why the New Testament author uses it.
SC9HEDED: Bediako's influential study of how early Christian and modern African theologians worked out Christian identity in relation to their cultural and religious heritage. He compares second-century writers, such as Justin and Tertullian, with twentieth-century African theologians, and argues that both faced the same question of integrating faith and culture.
CZ9V8ZHP: A chapter tracing the development of African theology during the twentieth century. It covers the move from missionary Christianity to African voices, and the key questions of African identity, culture, traditional religion and the gospel that shaped the discipline.
GW5VK2U5: Beker argues that apocalyptic expectation is central to Paul's thought. God's coming triumph over evil gives coherence to Paul's gospel, his ethics and his view of suffering. Beker urges the church to recover this hope instead of reducing Paul to individual salvation.
FUKXZUVA: Bell traces leadership through the whole biblical story and argues that leadership in Scripture is fundamentally service of God and friendship with him. Leaders are first servants and friends of God, and their leadership of others flows from that relationship.
PQA25NXZ: A standard methods textbook for anthropology and the social sciences. Bernard covers research design, sampling, interviewing, participant observation and other data collection, and both qualitative and quantitative analysis, with many practical examples.
5TZ726DF: The sixth edition of Bernard's standard text on research methods in anthropology. It covers research design, sampling, interviewing, participant observation, questionnaires and other data collection, and both qualitative and quantitative analysis, with updated examples.
F8HHHS7W: A practical guide to analysing qualitative data systematically. The authors explain approaches such as grounded theory, content analysis, schema and discourse analysis, and analytic induction, and show how to code texts, find themes and build models.
8AD3472E: Bickers, a bivocational pastor himself, argues that ministers who hold a second job are a vital model of ministry, not a second-class one. He addresses their practical challenges, including time, family, burnout, church expectations and leadership, and how to do both jobs well.
9R7PQ7AA: Bivin and Blizzard argue that many puzzling sayings of Jesus make sense when read against their Hebrew and Jewish background. They argue that the Gospels rest on Hebrew sources and illustrate how Hebrew idioms clarify Jesus' teaching.
5BHBRXI6: A collection of essays introducing the methods of New Testament study, including textual criticism, source, form and redaction criticism, social-scientific, literary and canonical approaches. Each chapter explains a method and assesses its strengths and weaknesses from an evangelical perspective.
4PEXQI3H: A short business fable about how organisations move from command and control to empowered teams. It sets out three keys: sharing information with everyone, creating autonomy through clear boundaries, and replacing hierarchy with self-directed teams.
8RFRQ2AU: The authors set out three keys for empowering people at work: share information with everyone, create autonomy through clear boundaries, and replace the old hierarchy with self-directed teams. They describe the journey through the stages of change in practical terms.
96EEM2VI: A business consultant, a pastor and a businesswoman present leadership as the Bible teaches it, built on servant leadership. Through a story of a sceptical business student, the book argues that a leader's heart, head and hands should all serve others.
7B7AKRQU: Blomberg makes a scholarly case that the Gospels are historically reliable. He examines miracles, the differences between the Gospels, the relationship between John and the Synoptics, and evidence from outside the Bible, and concludes that the Gospels deserve trust as historical accounts of Jesus.
6BRISVB4: Blomberg critiques the long-standing view that each parable makes only a single point. He argues that many parables make one point for each main character, and goes on to interpret the parables of Jesus on that basis.
RGRE9QEF: A commentary on the whole New Testament written by African American scholars. It reads each book in the light of the African American experience of slavery, segregation and the struggle for justice, alongside historical and literary study, and includes essays on reading the New Testament in that tradition.
76GR36GX: Bock's chapter explains how the New Testament authors use the Old Testament. He surveys the hermeneutical issues involved, the main schools of thought, and how these uses fit within the New Testament authors' view of Christ and the fulfilment of Scripture.
U2STNEUR: An evangelical reference dictionary on the Old Testament prophetic books. It has articles on each prophet and book, prophetic genres, themes, history and interpretive methods, with bibliographies.
Q9ZFJDJU: Bolsinger draws on the story of the Lewis and Clark expedition, which expected rivers and met the Rocky Mountains. He argues that church leaders must learn adaptive leadership in a changed, post-Christian world: leading change while staying connected to people and core values.
64WCJH7M: A major reference handbook on African theology. Its chapters cover the history and sources of African theology, key theologians, theological themes, and its engagement with culture, gender, politics, ecology and religion.
GSZCZHKT: A practical book on leadership in ministry. Bradford sets out twelve practices and principles, built around character, vision, relationships and service, that help pastors lead so that others want to follow.
JI5636I8: Braun and Clarke's practical guide to reflexive thematic analysis, the qualitative method they developed. They take the reader through the six phases, from becoming familiar with the data, coding and generating themes to reviewing, defining and writing them up, and discuss what makes the analysis good and how it differs from other approaches.
P6FMR93S: Brooke explores how the Dead Sea Scrolls illuminate the New Testament. He compares the Scrolls' interpretation of Scripture, beliefs and practices with those of the early Christians, while avoiding exaggerated claims of direct links.
BKMIKJNH: Brown's foundational text on Q methodology, a way of studying subjectivity systematically. He explains the theory, the construction of Q-sorts, factor analysis and interpretation, and shows how the method can be applied to political attitudes and beliefs.
S76S2M6E: Brown introduces biblical hermeneutics through speech-act and communication theory. She argues that Scripture is God's communication, so interpretation attends to what the authors were doing with their words in their contexts. She shows how this leads from understanding to faithful response.
H9TTBQ3Q: Brueggemann's major Old Testament theology is organised around courtroom imagery. Israel's "core testimony" about God (as creator, deliverer and covenant partner) stands in tension with its "countertestimony" of God's hiddenness and ambiguity. He argues that Old Testament theology should keep this dispute and plurality alive rather than resolve it.
3ZECZFJU: Bruner gives a critical evangelical assessment of Pentecostal teaching on the baptism in the Holy Spirit as a second experience after conversion. He surveys Pentecostal history and doctrine and then examines Acts and Paul. He concludes that the New Testament links the gift of the Spirit with faith in Christ, not with a subsequent stage.
4JENA9CC: A handbook surveying the current state of grounded theory, the qualitative method. International contributors discuss its history and variants (classic, Straussian and constructivist), its key practices, such as coding, memo-writing and theoretical sampling, and its use across disciplines.
IPGKMS2X: Bullock introduces Job, Psalms, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes and the Song of Songs. For each book he covers authorship, date, structure, literary features, theology and interpretation, and explains the nature of Hebrew poetry and wisdom.
5QIGVTAG: Burge examines the Holy Spirit in the Gospel and letters of John. He argues that for John the Spirit is closely bound to Jesus, and that the Spirit-filled community continues Jesus' presence and work. He also explores how this pneumatology shaped the community's life and conflicts.
4UAU2E2R: An introductory New Testament textbook that sets each book in its historical, cultural and religious world. It covers the Greco-Roman and Jewish background, Jesus and the Gospels, Paul and the other letters, and the church's development, with illustrations and primary sources.
C9GMA2IW: Caird's classic commentary on Revelation reads the book as a pastoral message for churches facing persecution. He interprets its symbolism against its Old Testament and first-century background, stressing the victory of the Lamb through suffering rather than predictions of the distant future.
XR6KNIVN: The authors present "theological action research", a partnership between academic researchers and church practitioners to reflect on practice. They introduce the idea that practice itself carries theology (in four "voices": normative, formal, espoused and operant), with case studies from churches and faith-based organisations.
AHP8I935: A dictionary article on the "Judaizers", the Jewish-Christian opponents Paul faced, especially in Galatia, who required Gentile believers to be circumcised and keep the law. It examines who they were, what they taught and how Paul answered them.
UAA84AVG: A classic short text on research design. Campbell and Stanley set out experimental and quasi-experimental designs and analyse the threats to internal and external validity that each design controls or leaves open. It remains a standard reference for evaluating research.
AJCTNEK9: Cargal argues that Pentecostals, who never fitted the fundamentalist-modernist debate, are well placed to engage postmodern hermeneutics. He suggests that Pentecostal readings of Scripture, which allow for multiple meanings and the Spirit's present work, find unexpected common ground with postmodern thought.
JRA5T7ST: Cartledge develops a practical theology from a charismatic standpoint that also uses empirical research. He proposes a dialectical method that brings together qualitative and quantitative study of experience and theological reflection, illustrated from charismatic practices such as worship and spiritual gifts.
QIAI6CHN: An annotated bibliography of Jewish literature from the intertestamental and early rabbinic periods, including the Apocrypha, Pseudepigrapha, Dead Sea Scrolls, Philo, Josephus and rabbinic texts. It guides students to editions, translations and key studies relevant to New Testament background.
NEQHGP3E: Charlesworth's standard two-volume collection of the Old Testament Pseudepigrapha in English translation. It contains Jewish and some Christian writings from roughly 200 BC to AD 200, including apocalypses, testaments, expansions of biblical stories, wisdom and psalms, each with an introduction and notes.
57A2C38D: Childs' mature statement of his canonical approach to biblical theology. He studies the Old and New Testaments as two distinct witnesses to Christ, each heard in its own voice, and then traces their themes together in theological reflection. The aim is to read Scripture as the church's canon.
NUB3ETKQ: Cho compares the Spirit and the kingdom of God in Luke and Paul. He argues that Luke presents the Spirit mainly as empowerment for mission and witness, while Paul links the Spirit with the life of the kingdom and new creation, and he proposes a way to relate the two.
4KU2SMCW: Clandinin and Connelly introduce narrative inquiry, a qualitative method that studies experience through stories. They explain the "three-dimensional" inquiry space of time, relationship and place, and describe fieldwork, field texts and writing narrative accounts, drawing on their own studies of teachers.
C45CE2H6: Clinton's self-study manual sets out his leadership emergence theory, an approach to how God develops Christian leaders over a lifetime. It explains the process items, phases and patterns in leadership development and gives exercises for readers to analyse their own development.
FZK885A8: Clinton goes through the Bible book by book and identifies the leadership lessons and values each one contains. He summarises the leadership principles found in Scripture as a resource for Christian leaders.
9DH54U3W: Clinton argues that leaders who finish well are those whose ministry rests on the Word of God. He explains what it means to be a Bible-centred leader and draws lessons from biblical and historical leaders who lasted.
3GMV8TKD: Clinton's popular account of how God develops a leader over a lifetime. He describes the stages of leadership development, from foundations and inner-life growth to ministry maturing and convergence, and the tests and lessons God uses in each.
UUG99U83: Cloud applies his work on boundaries to leadership. He argues that leaders get results by setting clear boundaries: on focus, emotional climate, relationships, thinking, team culture and on themselves. This creates conditions in which people and organisations thrive.
Z3ISCANJ: Cohen's standard introduction to Judaism from the Maccabean revolt to the Mishnah. He describes Jewish beliefs and practices, sects, the temple and synagogue, and the emergence of rabbinic Judaism. The third edition updates the discussion with recent scholarship.
8REC5DGU: Cohick describes the daily lives of women in the Greco-Roman and Jewish world of the first Christians: as daughters, wives, mothers, workers, patrons and religious participants. She draws on inscriptions, literature and material evidence and shows how this background illuminates the New Testament.
QI7UW2EG: An accessible introduction to statistics for students with little mathematical background. Coolidge covers descriptive statistics, probability, hypothesis testing, correlation, regression and common tests, emphasising understanding and interpretation over computation.
BQ5VEXCW: An article comparing ethnography and case study as research approaches. It sets out their similarities and differences in purpose, scope, data collection and analysis, and gives guidance on when each is appropriate.
PXTWXE2E: A leading textbook on research design. The Creswells explain the philosophical worldviews behind research and how to plan qualitative, quantitative and mixed-methods studies, covering literature reviews, theory, purpose statements, research questions, methods and ethics.
MUDNEB9Q: Croft and Butler argue that administration and delegation are part of pastoral shepherding, not a distraction from it. They show how pastors can organise church life, delegate wisely and develop others, so that people are better cared for and the pastor's time is freed for the Word and prayer.
A7UCMWIZ: Crowther examines servant leadership through biblical texts and leadership theory. She explores what Scripture teaches about leading as a servant and how those principles apply to leaders in contemporary organisations and churches.
PM2M56CB: Danby's classic English translation of the Mishnah, the foundational code of rabbinic Jewish law compiled around AD 200. It includes an introduction and explanatory notes, and is a key primary source for the Judaism of the New Testament era.
KAH9DT92: De Pree compares leadership to jazz, where the leader sets the theme and then lets others improvise. In reflective essays he discusses the qualities a leader needs (voice, touch, integrity and a concern for others) and shows how leadership is an art built on relationships.
58BXSKPE: De Vaux's classic study of the institutions of ancient Israel: family life, civil and political structures, the military and religious institutions such as priesthood, sacrifice, sanctuaries and festivals. He draws on both biblical texts and archaeology to explain how Israel lived.
58KNMSGT: DeSilva introduces each book of the Apocrypha, covering its content, historical setting, literary features and theological message. He shows its significance for understanding Second Temple Judaism, the New Testament and later church history. The second edition updates the scholarship.
9S5WQMZB: Dickson examines how Christian theology can be done authentically in Africa. He discusses the relation of the gospel to African culture and traditional religion, the use of the Bible, and themes such as Christology and the cross from an African perspective.
7UPU5QXM: An evangelical introduction to the Old Testament. For each book the authors discuss historical background, authorship and composition, literary analysis, theological message and how it points to the New Testament.
3J2QXQ9M: Dorr writes about and for pastors who support themselves with secular work while serving a church. He discusses the biblical and historical basis for bivocational ministry, its benefits and challenges, and how churches and denominations can support such pastors.
JQ6NF8QW: Douglas's influential essay on the dietary laws of Leviticus. She argues that clean and unclean animals reflect a system of classification: animals that do not fit their category are unclean, so the laws express ideas of wholeness and holiness rather than hygiene.
8SR8GNRK: Driver's classic introduction to the literature of the Old Testament, originally written in the late nineteenth century. Book by book, he sets out the contents and the critical views of authorship, sources and dates current in British scholarship of his time.
JUVTEXIT: An introduction to research methods for social psychology. Dunn explains the scientific method, research design, measurement, experiments, surveys and observation, data analysis and ethics, with examples from social psychological studies.
W2VHIT9Z: Dunn's influential study of baptism in the Holy Spirit in the New Testament. He argues that Spirit baptism is the gift of the Spirit that makes a person a Christian, part of conversion-initiation, rather than a second blessing after conversion. This challenges Pentecostal teaching.
9J8NZDX2: A widely used textbook on biblical interpretation. Duvall and Hays set out the "interpretive journey": grasp the text in its town, measure the width of the river separating that world from ours, cross the principlising bridge, and apply the text today. They apply this method to each genre of Scripture.
MCVQFWAJ: A shorter, more accessible version of Grasping God's Word. Duvall and Hays explain their interpretive journey from the meaning of a biblical text in its context to its application today, and apply it to the different kinds of literature in the Bible.
MW5MEB9R: Dyrness introduces theologians from Africa, Asia and Latin America and the questions they raise for Christian theology. The book helps Western readers engage emerging theological voices from the global church.
6XMHDZ42: A dictionary of theology written for the global church, with contributors from every continent. Its articles cover doctrines, movements and issues from global perspectives and show how theology is being done in different cultural contexts.
NHU53E96: Edington argues that bivocational ministry is not a new compromise but a return to the roots of ministry, seen in Paul and in the early church. He explores the opportunities it gives churches and pastors, and offers practical guidance for those serving in both ministry and other work.
B3KX6F3H: Ellington argues that Pentecostals have an experiential view of the authority of Scripture. They value the Bible because they experience God through it, not mainly because of rationalist doctrines of inerrancy, and he explores what this means for Pentecostal theology and hermeneutics.
MBGG685D: Ellis's classic study of how Paul quotes and uses the Old Testament. He examines Paul's citations, introductory formulas and text forms, compares them with Jewish exegesis of the time, and explains the theology of fulfilment behind them.
4W4P9UJW: An anthology of primary sources in translation from the Greek, Roman and Jewish world of the New Testament. Topics include religion, philosophy, politics, family life and slavery, and each text is introduced and connected to New Testament passages.
PKM868R6: A practical guide to writing fieldnotes in ethnographic research. The authors show how to jot notes in the field, turn them into full descriptions, record people's meanings, and analyse and write up fieldnotes into ethnographic texts.
H5VIU88M: Engelsviken traces the origin and development of the missio Dei concept. He shows how it began as a God-centred understanding of mission and how, in some European churches and missiology, it was later stretched until mission lost its connection to the church and evangelism.
WDFWE52K: Ervin, a Pentecostal scholar, responds to James Dunn's Baptism in the Holy Spirit. He argues from Luke-Acts and other texts that Spirit baptism is an empowering experience distinct from, and subsequent to, conversion.
6WGPHA6N: Escobar describes how the centre of Christian mission has shifted from the West to the global South. He argues that mission now comes "from everywhere to everyone", and discusses the new missionary realities, the biblical basis of mission and the challenges facing the church.
I7VHK4WI: An online research bibliography that guides students to key reference works, databases and resources for biblical and theological studies.
VNH9MMSS: Evans's guide to the ancient literature that forms the background to the New Testament, including the Old Testament Apocrypha and Pseudepigrapha, the Dead Sea Scrolls, Philo, Josephus, the targums, rabbinic writings and early Christian and Gnostic texts. For each he summarises contents and lists editions and studies.
E43AMEVF: Evans presents a systematic theology grounded in African American religious experience. He covers revelation, God, Christ, the Spirit, the church and last things, and shows how the history of slavery, struggle and faith shapes theological reflection.
JC2U9JS9: A comprehensive dictionary of the world of the New Testament. Its articles cover the Jewish, Greek and Roman history, literature, religion, social life and archaeology that help readers understand the New Testament.
Z6QTI7QK: Fee's major commentary on 1 Corinthians, revised in its second edition. He reads the letter as Paul's response to a church that was spiritually proud and divided, and explains its teaching on wisdom, sexuality, marriage, food offered to idols, worship, spiritual gifts and the resurrection.
ZRE5NRKF: A collection of Fee's essays on New Testament hermeneutics and Pentecostal interpretation. He discusses exegesis and its relation to the Spirit, the use of historical precedent (especially in Acts) for doctrine, and issues in reading Paul.
MZU5RJ2F: Fee's comprehensive study of every passage on the Holy Spirit in Paul's letters. He argues that for Paul the Spirit is God's own personal presence, the fulfilment of the promise of the new covenant, and central to Christian life and community, and then draws together Paul's theology of the Spirit.
5CNQ68DU: A shorter, more accessible version of Fee's God's Empowering Presence. He shows that the Spirit is at the centre of Paul's theology: God's personal presence who creates the people of God and empowers Christian life and community.
PFSAWJTT: Fee's commentary on the Pastoral Epistles. He reads them as letters addressing false teaching in Ephesus and Crete, and explains their instructions on church order, leadership, sound doctrine and Christian conduct.
HWSZ26SC: Fee's handbook on New Testament exegesis for students and pastors. He sets out step by step how to study a passage in Greek: establish the text, analyse grammar and words, study the historical and literary context, and move from exegesis to application.
3K383EAE: A landmark collection of essays by African American biblical scholars. It explores how race, culture and the experience of oppression shape biblical interpretation, and discusses Black presence in the Bible, the use of Scripture in slavery and liberation, and African American hermeneutics.
RGKFCZ7H: Fields introduces Black theology to evangelical readers by asking three questions: what Black theology is, whether evangelicals can learn from it, and how the church should respond. He gives a sympathetic but critical evangelical assessment.
P9UMVB8G: Fink presents a model for designing college courses around significant learning rather than content coverage. His taxonomy has six kinds of learning: foundational knowledge, application, integration, the human dimension, caring and learning how to learn. He then shows how to align goals, learning activities and assessment.
6GTIGCPN: Finzel draws on his experience in Christian organisations to describe ten common mistakes leaders make. They include putting tasks before people, being an autocrat and neglecting succession, and for each he shows how to avoid it.
B5NGXVXF: A collection of essays on biblical leadership for leaders in churches, organisations and the workplace. Contributors explore what Scripture teaches about leadership through biblical figures and themes, and apply it to everyday leadership.
AVZIHD8S: Foster's classic introduction to the spiritual disciplines. He presents them as means of grace that open us to God's transforming work: inward (meditation, prayer, fasting, study), outward (simplicity, solitude, submission, service) and corporate (confession, worship, guidance, celebration).
48HA8MWX: The first volume of the Soncino English translation of Genesis Rabbah, the classical rabbinic midrash on Genesis. It shows how the rabbis interpreted the opening chapters of Genesis verse by verse.
W59J5TF9: Freeman's evangelical introduction to the Old Testament prophets. He discusses the nature of prophecy and the prophetic office, and then introduces each prophetic book: its historical setting, message and interpretation.
N7Q388X8: A collection of Robert Greenleaf's previously unpublished private writings, edited by Frick and Spears. The essays show how Greenleaf's ideas of servant leadership developed and cover spirit, community, leadership and the inner life of the servant leader.
5FBIQZ2J: An anthology of key texts on biblical interpretation from the early church, translated with an introduction by Froehlich. It includes Origen, Tyconius, Augustine and others, and shows how early Christians read Scripture through literal, typological and allegorical approaches.
PNZ5FRI4: Gadamer's major work of philosophical hermeneutics. He argues that understanding is not a method but a dialogue, in which the interpreter's historical horizon fuses with that of the text through tradition and prejudice. The work has deeply influenced theological and biblical hermeneutics.
4EXP96PH: A practical guide to writing literature reviews in the social and behavioural sciences. The Galvans explain how to search for and select sources, analyse and synthesise them, and organise and write a coherent review, with many examples.
BIBRPX7H: A two-volume study edition of the non-biblical Dead Sea Scrolls with the Hebrew and Aramaic text facing an English translation. It is a standard reference for scholarly work on the Qumran texts.
RBJ35EIA: Garratt argues that organisational failure usually begins in the boardroom. He explains the role and responsibilities of a board of directors and shows how boards can develop the competence and focus to govern well.
6WF3PCGZ: Garrett asks how Christians should read the Old Testament. He surveys hermeneutical, schematic and theological approaches, including allegory, typology, covenant and dispensational schemes and Christological readings, assesses each, and proposes a way forward.
VCHTF6CI: A collection of essays by African scholars on reading the New Testament in Africa. Contributors address hermeneutical methods and engage issues such as culture, politics, gender, poverty and HIV and AIDS through New Testament texts.
GI3C4BPK: Yamauchi examines the evidence for Africa and Africans in the Bible and the ancient world: Cush, Ethiopia, Egypt and Black Africans in Greco-Roman sources. He critically assesses claims in Afrocentric scholarship and presents a careful historical account.
9HNQ4P5M: A textbook on research in missiology. Contributors explain how missiology draws on theology, the social sciences and history, and introduce research methods, including qualitative, quantitative, historical and biblical approaches, and how to integrate them in mission studies.
68THTJHZ: Glaser and Strauss's founding text on grounded theory. They argue that researchers should generate theory from data rather than only test existing theories, and they introduce constant comparison, theoretical sampling and saturation.
